title: Continuous realization and reductions of integral finite scalar models
statement: Work in the small-site and indexing universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite space $P$ (compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected), equip $\operatorname{Prof}/P$ with finite jointly surjective covering families. For a topological commutative ring $T$, write $R_T(Q\xrightarrow{a}P)=C(Q,T)$, with pointwise operations and pullback of continuous functions. Use ordinary internal $R_T$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and their ordinary uncompleted derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, and $O=\mathcal O_E$, with its valuation topology and a uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Give a finitely presented scalar $O$-module $B$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] the quotient topology from any finite presentation $O^m\to O^n\to B\to0$. This topology is independent of the presentation; $B$ is a compact Hausdorff profinite topological module and $B\cong\varprojlim_{k\ge1}B/\pi^kB$ as a topological module. The canonical map from the scalar model $R_O\otimes_{\underline O}\underline B$ (discrete constant underlines [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], ordinary scalar extension [def-sfb-modobj-extension]) to the sheaf $Q\mapsto C(Q,B)$ is an isomorphism. For any two such $B,C$, every morphism $v:B_{R_O}\to C_{R_O}$ is induced by a unique continuous map $\widetilde v:P\times B\to C$ whose restriction to each $\{p\}\times B$ is $O$-linear: on $Q\xrightarrow{a}P$ it sends $b$ to $[q\mapsto\widetilde v(a(q),b(q))]$. Its reduction induces maps of finite locally constant module bundles $B/\pi^kB\to C/\pi^kC$ on $P$, compatible with the actual quotient transitions. The canonical map identifies the sheaf kernel of $v$ with the ordinary inverse limit of the sheaf kernels of these reduction maps. Here a finite locally constant bundle is a finite disjoint union of products of clopen subsets of $P$ with finite discrete modules. No surjectivity or stabilization hypothesis is imposed on the reduction-kernel transitions. Zero modules and empty $P$ are allowed.

source.place: Example 3.1, Remark 3.2; agent finite-presentation and compact-reduction lemma. Compare Stacks 08YN (topology, proposition-projective-in-category-hausdorff-qc) for local lifting.

proof.text: Apply finite_module_topology for the module topology, continuous_scalar_comparison for the normalized scalar extension, and universal_section_morphism for the unique representing family. The quotient transition identity is proved directly by quotient induction. The reduction family is locally constant by evaluating finitely many chosen lifts in the finite quotient. The kernel comparison is bijective by the homeomorphism of the positive reduction limit for the source and injectivity of the corresponding limit map for the target; compatible sequences reconstruct a continuous section coordinatewise.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NF-aaf7c3a7c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all nine steps against the cited statements and the source; review.md has the details. The statement matches the base copy word for word, except for three added citations: def-sc-finitely-presented-module, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf and def-sfb-modobj-extension. Each exists and defines the notion it is cited for. The delivery has no new nodes. Source: Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach, Example 3.1 (continuous-map sheaf) and Remark 3.2 (constant-sheaf scalar extension). The rest of the proof is correctly marked agent-written. Steps 1–3: Smith normal form (exists_smith_normal_form_of_le leaf) and the DVR clauses give B ≅ O^r ⊕ ⊕O/π^e. The diagonal map O^n → product is a continuous surjection from a compact to a Hausdorff space, so it is a quotient map (compact-Hausdorff leaf). Lifting generators makes the topology independent of the presentation. The integers-profinite-tower node gives B ≅ lim B/π^k, and torsion summands are constant from k = e on. Step 4: the adjunction, the constant-sheaf property, the tensor universal property and Yoneda identify a(C(Q,O)⊗B) with the scalar model, and θ is the canonical map. Steps 5–6: the covers Q×_B O^n and Q×_N O^m are profinite and surjective, N is closed because B is Hausdorff, and the local-bijectivity leaf finishes. Step 7: evaluating v on the universal section over P×B (profinite by step 1) and pulling back along the graph gives the formula, with fibrewise linearity at point objects. Step 8: finitely many lifts give a finite clopen partition, and the transition squares commute. Step 9: kernel sequences glue through step 3 (applied to B and to C), and lem-sfb-modobj-kernels gives the module kernel; no Mittag–Leffler argument is used. Small cases checked: v = π on O (each reduction kernel is nonzero, transitions are zero, the limit is 0), O/π^e, zero modules, empty P, P a point. I found no duplicate in the DAG; I read normed-coefficient-realization, finite-discrete-encoded-constant-fp, admissible-scalar-model-cohomology, compact-adic-continuous-identification and procyclic-scalar-cochain-evaluation. Route: the unit uses nagata-sketch-comp-category, which covers the DVR lemma. I accept the declared tool_uses (integers-profinite-tower, continuous-abelian-profinite-sheaf, the sheafification leaf, the Lean-closed modobj-kernels) as generic black boxes that replace no unit step. No changes made.
